limitations_and_boundaries: All fibroblasts were cultured and serially passaged on rigid matrices before transfer to hydrogels; thus the role of mechanical memory could not be assessed.
The study does not assess the role of mechanical memory in influencing results.
The study used only in vitro and adoptive transfer models; direct human in vivo validation is lacking.

missed_core_items.source_excerpt: increased matrix stiffness enhances and YAP/TAZ knockdown attenuates procollagen I-positive cells (***P < 0.0001 by 1-way ANOVA, n = number of cells analyzed from 3 independent experiments) and soluble collagen production in cell culture medium, as measured with SirCol assay (**P < 0.05, by 1-way ANOVA from 2 independent experiments).

missed_core_items.source_excerpt: increasing matrix stiffness promotes and YAP/TAZ knockdown attenuates cell accumulation over 72 h, with the converse trend observed for caspase 3/7 activity (*P < 0.05 by t-test from 2 independent experiments).

missed_core_items.description: Effect of YAP/TAZ knockdown on contractile force generation (net contractile moment and peak tractions) on stiff vs soft matrices.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: increasing matrix stiffness enhances contractility, as measured by net contractile moment and peak tractions in traction force microscopy. YAP/TAZ siRNA knockdown selectively attenuates tractions on stiff matrices (***P < 0.0001 by 1-way ANOVA, n = number of cells analyzed from 2 independent experiments).

missed_core_items.description: Effect of YAP/TAZ knockdown on COL1A1 and FN1 transcript levels and EDA fibronectin protein in IPF fibroblasts on stiff vs soft matrices.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: increasing matrix stiffness promotes IPF ﬁbroblast gene expression of extracellular matrix transcripts COL1A1 and FN1. YAP/TAZ siRNA knockdown selectively attenuates matrix stiffness-promoted gene expression on stiff matrices (n = 2 independent experiments). Similarly, increasing matrix stiffness enhances expression of EDA ﬁbronectin (FN) protein, as measured by Western blot from cell lysates, and YAP/TAZ siRNA knockdown reduces EDA FN expression on pathologically stiff but not physiologically compliant matrix (n = 3 independent experiments).

missed_core_items.description: Effect of exogenous plasmin on procollagen I, α-SMA expression, and YAP/TAZ nuclear localization on stiff matrices.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: exogenous plasmin (0.1 U/ml) attenuates matrix stiffness-promoted procollagen I and α-smooth muscle actin (SMA) expression on stiff matrices in a fashion similar to YAP/TAZ siRNA knockdown. Plasmin also signiﬁcantly reduces the proportion of ﬁbroblasts with predominant nuclear localization of YAP/TAZ on stiff matrices; n = number of cells analyzed per condition.

missed_core_items.source_excerpt: inhibition of transforming growth factor (TGF)-β receptor with ALK5 inhibitor SB431542 (1 μM) or a pan anti-TGF-β antibody (10 μg/ml) has no effect on matrix stiffness-induced PAI-1 protein production or plasmin activity decrease in IMR-90-conditioned media (n = 2 independent experiments).

missed_core_items.description: Effect of YAP/TAZ knockdown on TGF-β-augmented PAI-1 expression on stiff vs soft matrices.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: exogenous TGF-β (2 μg/ml) potentiates matrix stiffness-promoted PAI-1 gene expression. YAP/TAZ siRNA double knockdown (YAPi/TAZi) ablates TGF-β effect on stiff matrices but has no effect on soft matrices (n = 2 independent experiments).

research_questions.statement: What are the molecular mechanisms by which matrix stiffness drives fibroblast activation and fibrosis?

provenance.text_excerpt: we show for the first time that fibroblast-expressing active YAP or TAZ are sufficient to drive a fibrogenic program in the lungs.

claims.statement: YAP and TAZ are sufficient to drive a fibrogenic response in vivo when activated in fibroblasts.

provenance.text_excerpt: these results identify YAP and TAZ as mechanoactivated coordinators of the matrix-driven feedback loop that amplifies and sustains fibrosis.

provenance.text_excerpt: disease-derived IPF fibroblasts in culture are indistinguishable from normal lung-derived fibroblasts in their levels of YAP/TAZ expression and remain fully able to reverse YAP and TAZ localization and function when cultured on physiologically soft matrices.

claims.statement: IPF fibroblasts in culture are indistinguishable from normal lung-derived fibroblasts in YAP/TAZ expression levels and remain responsive to matrix stiffness.

provenance.text_excerpt: the robust reversal of YAP and TAZ nuclear localization by relatively short-term culture on physiologically soft matrices suggests that lung fibroblasts, even those derived from pathologically stiffened lungs, retain the capacity to respond appropriately to changes in their mechanical environment.

claims.statement: YAP and TAZ nuclear localization is driven by matrix stiffness and is reversible when fibroblasts are cultured on soft matrices.

claims.statement: PAI-1 is a key downstream target of YAP/TAZ that mediates matrix stiffness-dependent fibroblast activation through regulation of plasmin activity.

experiments_or_tasks: Adoptive transfer of fibroblasts expressing constitutively active YAP (YAP5SA) or TAZ (TAZ4SA) into NSG mice to assess fibrogenic potential.
Immunofluorescence of YAP and TAZ localization in fibroblasts cultured on stiff (25 kPa) vs. soft (0.4 kPa) matrices.
Immunohistochemical staining of YAP and TAZ in IPF and normal lung tissue.
Measurement of PAI-1 expression and plasmin activity in response to matrix stiffness and YAP/TAZ knockdown.
Microarray analysis of stiffness-responsive transcripts in human lung fibroblasts and comparison with YAP overexpression targets in NIH3T3 cells.
siRNA knockdown of YAP and TAZ in fibroblasts on stiff vs. soft matrices, measuring matrix synthesis, contraction, proliferation, and apoptosis.

methods.name: Cell culture on polyacrylamide hydrogels
methods.protocol_description: Human lung fibroblasts (IMR-90) were cultured on polyacrylamide hydrogels of defined stiffness (0.4 kPa, 25 kPa) coated with collagen I. Cells were seeded at 5,000 cells/cm2 in DMEM with 10% FBS, then serum-starved overnight before experiments.

methods.name: Doxycycline-inducible Tet-On NIH3T3 cells
methods.protocol_description: Lentivirus generated using Lenti-X HTX packaging system to transduce rtTA-Advanced into NIH3T3 cells. Stable pools selected with G-418. Cells then infected with lentivirus expressing 3xFLAG-tagged human TAZ-4SA or YAP-5SA from pLVX-Tight-Puro. Stable cells grown with G-418 and puromycin.

methods.name: Adoptive transfer
methods.protocol_description: NSG male mice (8-12 wk old) injected via tail vein with 1x10^6 YAP5SA- or TAZ4SA-expressing fibroblasts in 300 µl PBS. Control groups received control fibroblasts or PBS. Mice given water or water with doxycycline (1 mg/ml) from day 0. Euthanized after 14 days. Left lung collagen measured by hydroxyproline assay; right lungs fixed, sectioned, stained with H&E or Masson's trichrome.

methods.name: Cell-derived matrix experiments
methods.protocol_description: Control or TAZ4SA-transduced NIH3T3 fibroblasts plated at 35,000 cells per well on 2% gelatin-coated coverslips. Fed every 48 h with doxycycline (0, 1, or 100 ng/ml). Decellularization at day 7 with PBS + 2% NH4OH + 0.5% Triton X-100. Matrix proteins solubilized with 5 M guanidine HCl + 0.1 M DTT. Protein content by BCA assay, normalized to cell number. Naïve cell adhesion: control NIH3T3 seeded on decellularized matrices for 4 h, nonadherent cells removed, adherent cells counted.

methods.name: siRNA transfection
methods.protocol_description: Cells were seeded on hydrogels in 24-well plates using DMEM with 1% FBS without antibiotics overnight, then exposed to 25 nM of each targeting siRNA or nontargeting siRNA. Cells were cultured for 3 days. Knockdown confirmed by RT-PCR after 72 h.

methods.name: Immunofluorescence
methods.protocol_description: Cells were fixed in formalin, permeabilized with 0.5% Triton X-100, blocked with 10% normal goat serum, incubated with primary antibodies (anti-YAP, anti-TAZ, anti-vinculin, anti-procollagen I) at 1:500, then secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488/546) at 1:500. F-actin stained with Alexa Fluor 546-Phalloidin, nuclei with Hoechst 33342.

methods.name: Soluble collagen assay
methods.protocol_description: Cell culture media collected 72 h after transfection, concentrated, and collagen concentration measured using Sircol Soluble Collagen Assay. Cell number determined by CyQUANT NF Cell Proliferation Assay. Collagen normalized to cell number.

methods.name: Apoptosis assay
methods.protocol_description: Apoptosis assessed using ApoONE Caspase 3/7 Activity Assay. Apoptosis ratio calculated by dividing ApoONE signal by CyQuant signal from parallel control wells.

methods.name: PAI-1 ELISA
methods.protocol_description: Cell culture media collected from cells on discrete stiffness gels in F12K DMEM with 10% FBS. PAI-1 concentration measured by Human PAI-1 Quantikine ELISA Kit, normalized to cell number.

methods.name: Plasmin activity assay
methods.protocol_description: Plasmin activity in cell culture media determined using SPECTROZYME PL chromogenic substrate. Absorbance measured at 405 nm.

methods.name: Traction force microscopy
methods.protocol_description: Polyacrylamide substrates with shear moduli 0.4 and 6.4 kPa prepared with fluorescent beads. Cells plated overnight, transfected with YAPi/TAZi, incubated 72 h. Bead displacement measured before and after trypsinization, traction fields computed using Fourier Transform Traction Microscopy.

methods.name: Quantitative PCR
methods.protocol_description: Cells lysed with RLT buffer, RNA isolated (RNeasy mini kit), quantified with RiboGreen. 50 ng RNA reverse transcribed with oligo(dT) using TaqMan reagents. qPCR with Power SYBR green, primers for YAP1, TAZ, SERPINE1, COL1A1, FN1, GAPDH. Ct values normalized to GAPDH.
